paper_title: Search for invisible axion dark matter with a multiple-cell haloscope
suggested_experiment_name: CAPP-9T (Center for Axion and Precision Physics Research, 9 Tesla)
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1, canonical axion-photon coupling
notes: Paper reports exclusion limit g_agamma ≳ 11.1 × g_KSVZ_agamma at 90% CL over mass range 13.0–13.9 μeV. The KSVZ model prediction for g_agamma is approximately 1.11 × 10^-16 GeV^-1 (dimensionless g_agamma ≈ 1.11 × 10^-16 in natural units, or ~1.11 × 10^-16 when expressed in GeV^-1 for the axion-photon coupling). The limit 11.1 × g_KSVZ corresponds to g_agamma ≳ 11.1 × 1.11 × 10^-16 ≈ 1.23 × 10^-15 GeV^-1. The mass range is converted from μeV: 13.0 μeV = 1.3 × 10^-5 eV, 13.9 μeV = 1.39 × 10^-5 eV. Local DM halo density assumed ρ_a = 0.45 GeV/cm³ (stated in text). This is the first results from a double-cell cavity haloscope, demonstrating a novel cavity design for high-mass axion searches.
